concerns.text: FR-003 defines the teacher distribution as the average logit distribution over all *unselected* rationales, which are also the data used to construct the Human Evaluation Proxy (FR-010/FR-015). This makes the validation target (Human Evaluation Proxy Score) dependent on the same rationales that serve as inputs to the AntiSD signal, creating a circular validation where the metric being evaluated is partially derived from its own predictor.

FR-010 states that the Human Evaluation Proxy Score is computed by comparing generated trajectories against a *human‑annotated subset of the unselected rationales*. Because the unselected rationales are also used to compute the teacher distribution (FR-003), the quality metric is not independent of the predictor, violating the requirement for an independent ground‑truth.

FR-011 requires computing a Pearson correlation between deliberation‑token frequency (continuous) and the Human Evaluation Proxy Score, which is a median of 1‑5 Likert ratings (ordinal). Pearson assumes interval‑scale data and linearity; a rank‑based correlation (Spearman) would be more appropriate for ordinal scores.

SC-001 conflates two distinct statistical procedures: it demands a positive Pearson correlation (r ≥ 0.3) *and* that this be “measured against the standard self‑distillation condition using the Wilcoxon signed‑rank test.” Correlation testing and Wilcoxon signed‑rank testing address different hypotheses and cannot be combined as described, indicating a methodological inconsistency.

FR-017 mandates the use of the Wilcoxon signed‑rank test for *all* statistical comparisons, yet the Idea Md section (Methodology sketch) mentions a paired t‑test. This discrepancy could lead to inappropriate test selection if not reconciled.
